title: Yankees place flamethrowing reliever Carlos Lagrange on injured list
content:
The bad injury news continues for the New York Yankees.

The Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders have placed right-handed reliever Carlos Lagrange on the seven-day injured list, the team announced Thursday. The extent of the injury has not been disclosed, but a team source told The Athletic that it is a shoulder injury and an MRI has been scheduled.

Regardless, the move is a setback for someone who was expected to be in the Yankees’ major league bullpen soon. Lagrange last pitched for the RailRiders on June 28, allowing four hits, two walks and five earned runs in 2/3 innings.

The 23-year-old started to transition from starting pitcher to reliever in early June, as the Yankees anticipated him making an impact in their bullpen before the trade deadline. That timeline may now be on pause.

Lagrange started to catch people’s attention earlier this year, after striking out Aaron Judge on a 102.6 mph fastball in spring training. That was the first sign that he was possibly becoming a key player to watch.

“The exciting thing for me was really being around him for the first time day by day (in spring training),” Yankees manager Aaron Boone said last month. “Seeing in person the competitor, how he works, and who he is. (All of that), coupled with — in spring training, you love to see a young guy go out there and perform and do well and relish the competition. So, there’s a lot of positives there. I think we all had the thought of maybe he could impact us in some way, shape or form throughout the year.”

New York’s bullpen could use an upgrade before next month’s trade deadline. Camilo Doval, who was expected to be a key reliever for the Yankees this season, has been a disappointment. At least one more high-leverage reliever could go a long way. Lagrange, whose fastball has been clocked at 103 mph, could have emerged as that option. That is now up in the air.
